compiled_state.description:
# Give Cloud the resilience and config-validation coverage DC gained

## Context

Epic e369 hardened the DC adapter against a real instance and produced a tier of coverage Cloud
never had. Cloud's tests grew from INCIDENTS THAT HAPPENED; DC's grew from CONFIGURATIONS THAT
DIFFER. The second kind generalises, and Cloud does not have it.

This story is the Cloud half of the parity work. It is lower priority than
[rebar:0fad-59f7-1605-4377] (Cloud's unpaginated whole-project readers) because Cloud is the mature,
live-exercised path — but each item below is a real asymmetry, not a symmetry exercise.

## The gaps, with what DC has for comparison

**1. No per-member 429 sweep.** DC's `test_dc_rate_limit_retry_heldout.py` walks EVERY mutating
transport member and asserts each fails on the first 429 — because retrying a mutation on an HTTP
error is the duplicate-issue class [rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03] fixed, and an enumeration is what
stops a later-added mutation inheriting a retry by omission. Cloud has
`test_retry_httperror.py` (5 tests) and one 429 path in
`state/test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py:352-368`, neither of which sweeps the member set.

**DC's property does NOT transfer uniformly, and assuming it does is the main risk in this item.**
Cloud has no single choke point; its mutations traverse FOUR distinct 429 behaviours across two
levels, all verified in the tree. Two are transport-level and DELIBERATELY OPPOSITE:

* **direct REST** (`AcliRestMixin._rest_urlopen_with_retry`) — "Does NOT retry on
  `urllib.error.HTTPError` (4xx / 5xx)" (`adapters/jira/acli_rest.py:50-52`). A 429 arrives as
  `urllib.error.HTTPError`. Here DC's property holds verbatim: exactly ONE attempt.
* **ACLI subprocess** (`acli_subprocess._run_acli`) — **already RETRIES a 429**, on purpose, via
  `_rate_limit_backoff` honouring `Retry-After`; `test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff`
  (`state/test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py:369`) asserts the call SUCCEEDS on retry. A 429 here is an
  exit code plus `429` in stderr, not an HTTP exception.

…and ABOVE both sits the reconciler's dispatch level, which is the part most likely to be missed —
and it is itself SPLIT IN TWO:

* **the retrying dispatch wrapper** — `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`
  (`dispatch_one.py:71`) catches `urllib.error.HTTPError` and, when `exc.code == 429`, records
  `Retry-After` and RETRIES (`dispatch_one.py:115-118`). So a REST mutation that makes exactly one
  attempt when its transport method is called DIRECTLY is nevertheless retried when reached the way
  production reaches it.
* **the explicitly NON-retrying apply phases** — `dispatch_apply_phases`, whose module docstring
  states it owns "the phases that do NOT funnel their Jira writes through
  `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`". These include real mutations:
  `_update_one_apply_reporter` (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:96`) and
  `_update_one_dispatch_comments` (`:147`, the single-attempt comment dispatch). A 429 here is a
  FOURTH behaviour — neither the subprocess backoff nor the dispatch-wrapper retry applies — and
  existing coverage (`test_comment_single_attempt.py`) pins attempt count for ONE member, not a
  sweep.

So "every mutating member fails on the first 429" is TRUE for a raw REST transport method called
directly, TRUE again for the non-retrying `dispatch_apply_phases` mutations, and FALSE for both the
subprocess seam and anything routed through the retrying dispatch wrapper. **An attempt-count
assertion is therefore meaningless unless it names the BOUNDARY it measures at.** Writing the DC assertion across all four would either fail immediately
or pressure someone into deleting an intentional, tested backoff. This story must establish the
split FIRST and assert a per-layer property — and it must not fold in a behaviour change (below).

**The two retries named above are KNOWN and DELIBERATE — they are not the bug trigger.** Both
`_run_acli`'s rate-limit backoff and `_call_with_retry`'s 429 branch are already implemented,
tested and documented, so "a mutation is retried on a 429" is not by itself a finding; the
enumeration will hit them by construction. The bug-filing trigger is NARROWER: a mutating member
retried on a 429 at a layer where that retry is NOT already explicitly tested and documented — an
UNDOCUMENTED or newly-discovered retry path. That is the [rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03] duplicate
class. If one is found, file a linked bug with the evidence and do NOT "fix" it inside this test
story. Separately, if the enumeration shows a KNOWN retry applying to a mutation in a way nobody has
evaluated for duplicate-write safety, record that assessment on this ticket — as a finding, not as a
code change.

**2. No config-validation tier.** DC asserts a non-HTTPS base URL is rejected, that the insecure
override warns, that malformed config propagates, and that a missing credential fails loudly rather
than going anonymous (`test_jira_dc_config_settings.py`, `test_dc_pat_required_heldout.py` — the
latter exists because bug cd78 was exactly a silent fall-back to ANONYMOUS access). Cloud has no
equivalent. Whether Cloud CAN go anonymous is itself unestablished and worth answering.

**3. The probe's resolved-status set is not runtime-configurable.** `adapters/jira/probe.py:39` pins
`frozenset({"Resolved","Done","Cancelled"})`; DC threads `resolved_statuses` from settings and
tests it. Cloud's `probe_remote` also re-resolves env itself rather than using the transport's
configured session.

**"Is it deliberate?" is already answered — do NOT re-open it.** `probe.py`'s module docstring
(`:20-25`) states that J2 moved the pure classifier to `adapters/jira_family/probe.py` taking the
status set as a PARAMETER, and that `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` "is Cloud/DIG's *configured value* (a
self-hosted Data Center workflow can name its resolved states anything), so it stays defined here".
So it is documented as deliberate at the definition site, and an AC satisfied by "document it" would
be satisfied by doing nothing. The remaining OPEN question is narrower and is the only one this item
answers: **does a Cloud deployment whose workflow uses non-standard resolved-status names need a
runtime config hook** (as DC has), or is the per-deployment constant genuinely sufficient? Record
THAT decision with its rationale; if a hook is needed, file it as its own ticket.

**4. `search_user_by_email` degradation is unasserted on DC** (the mirror-image item, kept here so
the pair is not split). `outbound_assignee.py:33-37` resolves the user-search method by NAME STRING
across three aliases; DC provides none of them, so `_bootstrap_account_id_via_user_search` returns
`None` and the path degrades to string matching. That degradation is probably correct — DC has no
accountId concept — but nothing asserts it, so an accidental rename on the Cloud side would look
like the same silence.

## Approach

Take these in the order above; 1 and 2 carry the risk, 3 is an investigation that may produce a
ticket rather than a test, 4 is a one-test pin.

**Port the PROPERTY, not the test — and note the property is PER-LAYER.** Cloud's retry lives in a
different place from DC's, so a copied test would assert the wrong seam. What must survive the port
is the ENUMERATION — that every mutating member is named explicitly, because an ellipsis is how the
next mutation inherits a retry.

**Step 0 for item 1, before any test is written:** enumerate every mutating member of Cloud's
transport and classify each on BOTH axes, by reading bodies rather than inferring from names:

1. **transport seam** — one of THREE: ACLI subprocess (`_run_acli`); pooled direct REST
   (`_rest_urlopen_with_retry` / `_direct_rest_post_raw` / `_direct_rest_put_raw`); or **bare
   `urllib.request.urlopen`**, which bypasses `_rest_urlopen_with_retry` entirely and therefore does
   not even inherit its transient-fault retry — `acli_cli_ops.update_priority`
   (`acli_cli_ops.py:396`, urlopen at `:437`) is a confirmed instance, reached in production because
   `AcliClient.update_issue` delegates to the free function `update_issue` (`acli.py:374`), which
   calls `update_priority` when `priority` is among the changed fields (`acli.py:180`). A member with
   more than one leg (e.g. a REST leg and a subprocess leg) is called out as such.
2. **dispatch level** — which of THREE the reconciler uses: the retrying wrapper
   `dispatch_one._call_with_retry` (`dispatch_one.py:71`), which adds a 429 retry ON TOP of
   whatever the seam does; the explicitly non-retrying apply phases in `dispatch_apply_phases`
   (`_update_one_apply_reporter:96`, `_update_one_dispatch_comments:147`); or no dispatch wrapper at
   all. Determine this by reading the call site, since the module split is by RETRY POLICY, so the
   answer is not inferable from the member's own body.

**Completeness check for the table, run and recorded alongside it** — the table gates the whole
item, so its coverage must be demonstrated, not asserted. Enumerate the candidate surface with a
concrete command and account for EVERY name it returns:

    git grep -nE "^(    )?def [_a-z]" -- \
      src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py \
      src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_graph.py \
      src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_rest.py \
      src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py

Three things about that pattern are deliberate, and each one is a way the table can look complete
while omitting a writer:

* it matches BOTH indented class methods AND module-level free functions;
* it includes `_`-PREFIXED names — `acli_graph._add_label_impl:144` and `_remove_label_impl:204` are
  mutating, as are the `_direct_rest_*` helpers in `acli_rest.py`, and a `def [a-z]` pattern would
  emit none of them, so the "every name it returns is classified" rule would be satisfied vacuously;
* `acli_cli_ops.py` is in the file list, because `AcliClient` delegates real mutations to free
  functions there (`create_issue:147`, `update_priority:396`, `add_comment:469`).

Record that raw output as a REPO ARTIFACT beside the table (in the sweep module's header comment, where the table lives) and mirror it onto the ticket. Every name in it is either classified in the
table or explicitly marked NON-MUTATING with a one-line reason — no name may be silently absent.
Cross-check the mutating set against DC's enumerated list in `test_dc_rate_limit_retry_heldout.py`
and record any member DC sweeps that Cloud's table lacks, or vice versa, with the reason.

The table decides, per member, which property is asserted and at which boundary it is observed — and
a member can legitimately have DIFFERENT correct answers at the two levels (one attempt raw, retried
when dispatch-wrapped).

## Scope

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — Cloud 429 sweep, Cloud config-validation tests, a DC
  user-search-degradation pin.
- an investigation note (or a linked bug) on the Cloud probe's hardcoded resolved statuses.
- the per-member seam classification table for item 1 (recorded on the ticket, not in code).
- No production change intended. Items 1 and 3 may each produce a linked BUG — item 1 only if a
  mutating member is retried on a 429 at a layer where that retry is NOT already tested and
  documented (the two known deliberate retries do not count), item 3 if the hardcoded
  resolved-status set is an accident — and in both cases the fix is its own ticket, never folded in
  here.

## Testing

The 429 sweep must assert the ATTEMPT COUNT per member, not merely that an exception escaped — an
implementation that retried and then re-raised satisfies a raises-only assertion having issued the
write twice. This is the same correction being applied to DC's own sweep in
[rebar:2944-dd3f-e982-4359]; do not copy that mistake forward.

**The instrument differs per seam, and a single patch point covers only half the members** — a sweep
that patches `urllib.request.urlopen` is blind to subprocess mutations, and one that patches
`acli_subprocess._run_acli` is blind to REST mutations, while either LOOKS complete because every
member still raises. So:

* POOLED REST-seam members, called DIRECTLY on the transport (not through the dispatch wrapper) —
  observe attempts at the urlopen boundary; inject a 429 as `urllib.error.HTTPError`; assert EXACTLY
  ONE attempt (no retry), matching `acli_rest.py:50-52`.
* BARE-`urlopen` members — `acli_cli_ops.update_priority` (`:396`, urlopen at `:437`) bypasses
  `_rest_urlopen_with_retry`, so it has no retry of its own: assert EXACTLY ONE attempt there too.

  **One patch point covers both, and per-module patching is NOT a real isolation mechanism.** Both
  `acli_rest.py` (`:23`) and `acli_cli_ops.py` (`:24`) do `import urllib.request` — a MODULE-object
  binding — so both resolve `urlopen` at call time through the same shared `urllib.request` object.
  Patching it once affects both; `mutate/test_acli_cross_mixin_binding.py:160` already relies on
  exactly that, calling it "the process-wide `urllib.request.urlopen` (a shared singleton)". So
  patch it once and distinguish the seams by WHICH MEMBER was invoked and what the captured request
  looks like — not by which module the patch was applied through. Coverage of both seams must
  therefore be proven by ENUMERATION (every member in the table has a case) rather than by any
  assumed namespace separation.
* the DISPATCH-WRAPPED path — the same members reached through `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`
  DO retry a 429 by design (`dispatch_one.py:115-118`). Assert the retry is bounded and honours
  `Retry-After`; do NOT assert one attempt here. This is the layer where "is a MUTATION being
  retried on a 429?" is actually decided, so it is the layer the bug-filing trigger below applies to.
* subprocess-seam members — observe attempts at the `_run_acli`/`Popen` boundary; inject a 429 as
  the exit-code + `429`-in-stderr shape the existing test uses; assert the OBSERVED, INTENDED
  behaviour (a bounded retry honouring `Retry-After`, per
  `state/test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py:369`) rather than one attempt — and record whether that
  retry applies to a MUTATION, which is the bug-filing trigger above.

Each seam's sweep must be MUTATION-CHECKED at its own instrument: make one member issue an extra
attempt at that boundary and confirm THAT seam's sweep goes red — proving the sweep is not blind to
the half it is supposed to cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] every MUTATING Cloud transport member is enumerated explicitly — no ellipsis, no sampling —
      and classified on BOTH axes: transport seam (ACLI subprocess / pooled direct REST / bare
      `urllib.request.urlopen`) and dispatch
      level (retrying `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`, the explicitly NON-retrying
      `dispatch_apply_phases` phases, or no wrapper). The table ALSO carries, for every member that
      reaches a mutation through a KNOWN deliberate retry (`dispatch_one._call_with_retry` or
      `_run_acli`'s rate-limit backoff), a "Duplicate-write safe? [reason]" column recording the
      duplicate-write assessment for that member — so the assessment is a repo artifact, not a
      tracker-only note. The table lands as a REPO ARTIFACT — the sweep test module's own enumeration
      plus a header comment carrying the per-member classification and that duplicate-write-safety
      column, which is where a reviewer will look — and is mirrored onto this ticket
- [ ] the table's COMPLETENESS is demonstrated, not asserted: the enumeration command from Step 0 is
      run, its raw output recorded beside the table, and every name it returns is either classified
      or marked NON-MUTATING with a reason — plus the DC cross-check for members present on one side
      and missing on the other
- [ ] each POOLED-REST and each BARE-`urlopen` mutating member, invoked DIRECTLY on the transport, is
      asserted to make EXACTLY ONE attempt under a 429, observed at the shared process-wide
      `urllib.request.urlopen`, with one case PER MEMBER from the table — `acli_cli_ops.update_priority`
      explicitly among them
- [ ] the DISPATCH-WRAPPED path is covered separately: reached through
      `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`, a 429 IS retried by design (`dispatch_one.py:115-118`), so the
      assertion there is a BOUNDED retry honouring `Retry-After` — not one attempt
- [ ] each subprocess-seam mutating member is asserted against its ACTUAL intended 429 behaviour —
      the bounded `Retry-After` backoff in `_run_acli` — observed at the `_run_acli` boundary. This
      criterion is NOT satisfied by asserting one attempt there, because
      `test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff` proves the retry is deliberate
- [ ] mutations reached through the NON-retrying `dispatch_apply_phases` path
      (`_update_one_apply_reporter`, `_update_one_dispatch_comments`) are asserted to make exactly
      one attempt under a 429 — extending `test_comment_single_attempt.py`'s single-member pin to
      the sweep
- [ ] if a MUTATING member is retried on a 429 at a layer where that retry is NOT already tested and
      documented, a linked bug is filed with the evidence. The two KNOWN deliberate retries
      (`_run_acli`'s rate-limit backoff, `_call_with_retry`'s 429 branch) do NOT by themselves
      trigger a bug; where one applies to a mutation, the duplicate-write assessment is RECORDED in
      the sweep module's "Duplicate-write safe? [reason]" table column (the authoritative repo
      artifact) and mirrored onto this ticket — never ticket-only. This story changes NO retry
      behaviour either way
- [ ] Cloud rejects a non-HTTPS base URL, or the test records that it deliberately does not
- [ ] Cloud's behaviour on a MISSING credential is asserted: it must fail loudly, or the test pins
      that it does not and a bug is filed (this is bug cd78's shape on the other adapter)
- [ ] the OPEN question on the Cloud probe's resolved-status set is answered: whether a Cloud
      deployment using non-standard resolved-status names needs a runtime config hook as DC has, or
      whether the per-deployment constant suffices. The DECIDING CRITERION is whether a Cloud
      deployment can rename its resolved-status workflow states WITHOUT a rebar code change: if
      `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` is compiled into the adapter and no per-tenant override path exists, a
      deployment with non-standard names is mis-probed and a runtime hook is warranted (file it);
      if such names cannot occur on Cloud (a documented workflow constraint) the constant suffices.
      The answer lands as a REPO ARTIFACT, not only a ticket comment — a comment at `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` in `adapters/jira/probe.py` recording the
      decision and citing this ticket id (plus the follow-up ticket id if a hook is needed) — so a
      reviewer can find it without the tracker. Re-documenting it as merely "deliberate" does NOT
      satisfy this: `probe.py:20-25` already says so, and an AC already true on an unmodified tree is
      not a criterion
- [ ] a test pins that DC exposes none of `_USER_SEARCH_METHODS` and that the bootstrap degrades to
      the string-match path rather than raising
- [ ] each new test is MUTATION-CHECKED. "Mutation-checked" here means a CONCRETE MANUAL mutation,
      not a mutation-testing tool: for each new test, apply the named perturbation below, run that
      test module, record it RED with its pass/fail counts, revert, record it GREEN again. Both
      verdicts go in a REPO-VISIBLE place — the commit/Gerrit change description of the change that
      adds the tests, listing per test the mutation applied and the RED/GREEN pass-fail counts — as
      well as on this ticket, so the evidence is reviewable from the change itself and survives
      independently of the tracker. The named mutations are: for a REST-seam sweep, make one member retry
      once at the urlopen boundary (the `== 1` attempt assertion must go red); for a subprocess-seam
      sweep, SUPPRESS the retry outright — cap `_run_acli`'s attempt loop at one, or make it re-raise
      on a 429 exit without looping — so the ATTEMPT-COUNT assertion goes red. Note what does NOT
      work: making `_rate_limit_backoff` return `None` does not remove the retry at all, because
      `acli_subprocess.py:429` is
      `_backoff_sleep(rl_delay if rl_delay is not None else 2 ** (attempt + 1))` — a `None` merely
      swaps `Retry-After` for a uniform exponential delay and the call is still retried;
      for the non-HTTPS-URL test, FIRST establish whether Cloud has a scheme rejection at all —
      `_validate_reconciler_tls` (`_config_schema.py:78`) is invoked only from
      `ReconcilerConfig.__post_init__` (`:437`, invoking `_validate_reconciler_tls` at `:438`), and Cloud's `AcliClient` / settings resolution has
      no scheme check of its own, so the likely answer is that Cloud does NOT reject `http://`. If it
      DOES reject, disable that rejection and confirm the test goes RED. If it does NOT, the test is
      absence-documenting, and its mutation check is the inverse: ADD a scheme assertion to the
      production path, confirm the absence-documenting test goes RED, then revert — record which of
      the two cases applied. Do NOT hunt for a non-existent hook, and do NOT add one permanently
      (a production change, out of scope); for the missing-credential test, make
      the production path proceed WITHOUT raising when the credential is absent (the cd78
      anonymous-fallback shape) and confirm the test goes RED; for the `_USER_SEARCH_METHODS`
      degradation pin, add one of the three alias names to the DC stub and confirm the pin goes RED;
      for the DISPATCH-WRAPPED-path test, unbound the retry in `dispatch_one._call_with_retry` (e.g.
      remove the `if attempt < max_retries:` guard so it loops without limit, or force `retry_after`
      to be ignored) and confirm the BOUNDED-retry / `Retry-After`-honouring assertion goes RED, then
      revert; for the NON-retrying `dispatch_apply_phases` sweep, add a second call to the transport
      member inside `_update_one_apply_reporter` (or `_update_one_dispatch_comments`) so it retries
      once under a 429 and confirm the `== 1` attempt assertion goes RED, then revert.
      Every named perturbation above must be one that makes its test FAIL — a step that merely
      exercises the passing path is not a mutation check

file_impact.reason: NEW: enumerated per-member Cloud 429 sweep (REST/bare-urlopen one-attempt, dispatch-wrapped bounded retry, subprocess-seam bounded retry, non-retrying apply-phases one-attempt) + classification header table
NEW: Cloud non-HTTPS base-URL + missing-credential behaviour pins (absence-documenting where Cloud lacks the check)
NEW: pin that DC exposes none of _USER_SEARCH_METHODS and the bootstrap degrades to string-match
add a decision comment at RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES answering the item-3 config-hook question (repo artifact)

compiled_state.title: Cloud resilience + config-validation coverage, matching DC's
